title: Generic rank determines the coefficient ideal and lower Fitting vanishing
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and suppose $B\otimes_R E$ is an integral domain for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and every field extension $E/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Fix $R$-linear maps $i:B\to F=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in A}R$ and $\rho:F\to B$ with $\rho i=1_B$. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], $h\in R$, and $r\geq0$. For each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ let $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ be the inverse image of the zero prime of $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $M_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}\cong B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}^{\oplus r}$ when $h\notin\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization, def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Put $J=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M)$ using [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], and let $C\subset R$ be the ideal generated by all coordinates of all $i(j)$ for $j\in J$. Then $J$ has finitely many generators $j_1,\ldots,j_t$, and $C$ is generated by the finitely many nonzero coordinates of $i(j_1),\ldots,i(j_t)$. The ideal $I=hC$ is finitely generated and satisfies $V(I)=V(h)$. If $r>0$, then $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M)B_h=0$.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $B^m\xrightarrow{A}B^n\xrightarrow{\pi}M\to0$ by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], and put $d=n-r$ when $n>r$. Every row of $\ker\pi$ is a $B$-linear combination of the $m$ relation rows of $A$. Expand a $d$-row minor of such combinations by the determinant formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]: each term is a coefficient times a minor of $d$ chosen relation rows, and terms with a repeated row cancel in pairs by interchanging the corresponding permutation indices. Therefore [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] identifies $J$ with the ideal generated by the finite list of $d$-minors of this finite relation matrix. If $d>m$, all terms have repeated rows and the list is empty, giving $J=0$. If $n\le r$, the same cited definition gives $J=B$, generated by $1$. Denote the resulting finite list by $j_1,\ldots,j_t$.

proof.text: Write $i(j_k)=\sum_\alpha c_{k\alpha}e_\alpha$ with finite support and let $C_0$ be the ideal generated by these finitely many nonzero coefficients. Clearly $C_0\subseteq C$. For $b\in B$, the $R$-linear endomorphism $T_b=i\circ(b\cdot-)\circ\rho$ of $F$ satisfies $T_bi(j_k)=i(bj_k)$ because $\rho i=1$. Thus the $\beta$-coordinate of $i(bj_k)$ is $\sum_{\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}i(j_k)}c_{k\alpha}(T_be_\alpha)_\beta$, which belongs to $C_0$. Every $j\in J$ is a finite sum $\sum_kb_kj_k$, so linearity gives every coordinate of $i(j)$ in $C_0$. Hence $C=C_0$. The ideal $I=hC$ is generated by the finite list $hc_{k\alpha}$; this calculation also covers the empty list.

Fix $\mathfrak p$ with $h\notin\mathfrak p$, and put $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$. The fibre is a nonzero domain by hypothesis, so its zero ideal has prime inverse image $\mathfrak q$. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change] (2) for $B\to B_\mathfrak q$, $JB_\mathfrak q$ is the index-$r$ ideal of $M\otimes_BB_\mathfrak q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] with $S=B\setminus\mathfrak q$, $\ell_M:M\to M_\mathfrak q$ and $\ell_N=1:B_\mathfrak q\to B_\mathfrak q$ (a localization, as $S$ already acts bijectively): the map $M\otimes_BB_\mathfrak q\to M_\mathfrak q$, $m\otimes b\mapsto bm/1$, is a localization at $S$ of a module on which $S$ acts bijectively, hence an isomorphism by (b) and (c). So $JB_\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Fit}_r(M_\mathfrak q)$. Use the given isomorphism $B_\mathfrak q^r\cong M_\mathfrak q$ as generating surjection: the same node defines its index-$r$ ideal to be the unit ideal. Thus $JB_\mathfrak q=B_\mathfrak q$ and $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$: otherwise every element of the extended ideal has numerator in $\mathfrak q$, so cannot equal $1$ in the local ring, by the fraction equivalence in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Choose $j\in J\setminus\mathfrak q$. If $r>0$, this surjection has zero kernel, so every $1$-minor defining $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M_\mathfrak q)$ is zero. Consequently $\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M)B_\mathfrak q=0$, again by base change.

For this prime $\mathfrak p$, suppose $C\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Every coordinate of $i(j)$ then maps to zero in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, hence $i(j)\otimes1=0$ in $F\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$: expand the finite sum in the displayed basis of $F$. Put $R^*=R_h$ and $B^*=B_h$. Identify $R_h\otimes_RB$ with $B_h$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor], using symmetry of the factors. The flatness theorem [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] and finite-presentation theorem [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1) show that $R^*\to B^*$ is flat and finitely presented. A prime of $R_h$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ avoiding $h$, with the same residue field: the prime is the set of fractions with numerator in $\mathfrak p$, its contraction is $\mathfrak p$, and its local ring is $R_\mathfrak p$ by the mutually inverse fraction maps. For any field extension $E/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, the maps $(b/h^n)\otimes e\mapsto b\otimes h^{-n}e$ and $b\otimes e\mapsto(b/1)\otimes e$ identify $B_h\otimes_{R_h}E$ with $B\otimes_RE$. Therefore the required geometric domain condition holds for $R^*\to B^*$. Its fibre-generic prime is $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}B_h$, and $(B_h)_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}B_h}\cong B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$: both rings invert exactly the elements needed for these successive localizations, since $h\notin\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$. These identifications follow explicitly by $b/h^n\mapsto b/h^n$ in each local ring.

Assume $r>0$ and write $L=\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(M)$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-generic-localization-intersection] to $R_h\to B_h$, whose hypotheses were checked in step 5. It gives an injection $B_h\to\prod_{\mathfrak p\in D(h)}B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$ with the maps identified there. Step 3 says that every element of $L$ maps to zero in every factor. Consequently every element of the extended ideal $LB_h$ maps to zero in every factor as well: it is a finite sum of products of images of elements of $L$ and elements of $B_h$. Injectivity gives $LB_h=0$, as asserted. This argument does not infer vanishing from the reduction modulo primes and does not assume that $R$ is reduced.
